commits.message:
Map Custom devnet protocol network to testnet network id 0 in lucid-midgard

Caught during live isolated-chain devnet verification of midgard-user-cli send: knownNetworkId in lucid-midgard threw 'unsupported protocol network' for Custom networks.

Run the ingress flood test after the test that takes the node away

Node CI's "Operator compose stacks" job has failed since 55613ec58 at
public-ingress.test.mjs:492 with "429 !== 503". That commit made the
socket-gone test ask for /init while the node is down. /init is one of the
routes nginx rate-limits per address, and the test before it had just
drained that rate with 60 health checks, so nginx refused /init for rate
before it tried the node.

The nginx configuration is as designed. The flood test now runs last, so no
test meets the rate it leaves behind. No assertion changes.

Verified (rerun here, nginx 1.30.6):
- before the move: node --test demo/midgard-node/scripts/public-ingress.test.mjs
  fails at line 492 with 429 !== 503, as in CI
- after: the same command, 11 runs, each 10 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
- eslint and prettier on the file

Not verified:
- CI's own nginx build; the failure and the fix were reproduced with a local
  nginx only

Give the devnet Postgres room for a run of several nodes

A devnet-stack run's nodes and DA committee share one Postgres server. With
the image's default of 100 connections, a run of three nodes had 102 in use:
nodes, committee members and journey steps were refused with "sorry, too
many clients already" and retried.

The server now starts with max_connections=400.

Verified (rerun here):
- the postgres service started alone from this compose file answers
  "show max_connections" with 400
- prettier --check on the compose file

Not verified:
- a run of several nodes was not repeated with the raised limit

End a merge another node already made as a skip, not a failure

Merges are permissionless and every node attempts the oldest block's merge.
On a network of several nodes each merge has one winner; every other node's
transaction is refused for spent inputs. The losers logged three ERROR lines
and failed the tick, although the block was merged.

The merge now passes the submit path's lost-race probe (added for the
scheduler in 3130eb855): the state a merge is sent for is "the landed state
queue no longer holds the block", the predicate the merge fiber already waits
on after its own merge. A refused merge whose block is gone logs the lost
race at info and returns skipped_merge_candidate_changed. Nothing else about
merge submission changes.

mergeSubmitRecoveryOptions now builds the whole recovery from the merge's
facts (the builder computed the validity slot and defer evidence only to
hand them over), which keeps the builder under its line cap.

Verified (rerun here):
- tsc --noEmit and eslint for midgard-node
- the tests the two files reach (contrib test --package midgard-node
  --related): 0 failed
- a three-node devnet (local-devnet-testing) at this commit: the nodes that
  lose a merge log the lost race at info, no ERROR line

Not verified:
- no emulator regression test. The merge emulator harness runs one node with
  one merge wallet and one intent journal, so a rival merge built there is
  this node's own transaction, which the submit path answers as a resend
  before it asks the lost-race probe.

Log the ledger a node installs at a snapshot start

A node that took its ledger from a peer logged nothing about it: the log
did not say the node had started from a snapshot, at which confirmed head,
or which peer served it. It now logs one line after the install with the
head, the UTxO root, the number of entries and the serving peer, or that
the ledger was empty and no peer was asked.

Verified (rerun here):
- Devnet with three operators' nodes: node 3, restarted with its database
  and ledger store removed, logged "ledger take-in: installed the ledger of
  5eb5a472... (e602094a...): 9 entries from snapshot peer 12D3KooWDsCar..."
  (the stack's node), and its confirmed and working ledgers matched the
  other two nodes'.
- tsc --noEmit and eslint on midgard-node.

Not verified:
- The empty-ledger wording; no run started a node at an empty confirmed
  ledger after this change.

Read the operator lists again after the activation wait

An activation read the registered, active and retired operator lists once,
before the registration transaction, and built from that read after waiting
out the registration delay. A block commitment spends its operator's active
node, so when the operator a new key is inserted behind committed a block
during the wait, the activation named a spent input and the L1 rejected it
(BadInputsUTxO).

Seen on a devnet with three operators: operator 3's activation was rejected
after operator 2 committed a block during its 142 s wait. A rerun, which had
no wait left, was accepted.

The activation now reads the nodes it spends or cites after the wait. An
activation into the empty active set does not wait and keeps its one read.
A transaction that lands between that read and the submit still gets the
activation rejected; the command can be rerun and resumes at the activation.

Verified (rerun here):
- tests/submit-wait-for-tip-emulator.test.ts, "activates behind
  active-operators nodes that other transactions re-created during the
  wait": 0 passed, 1 failed ("Could not spend UTxO") with the read from
  before the wait kept; 1 passed with the change. Whole file: 8 passed,
  0 failed, 0 skipped.
- contrib test --package midgard-node --related on the three changed source
  files: 171 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped in 23 files.
- tsc --noEmit and eslint on midgard-node.

Not verified:
- A devnet activation with the change; the run had no further operator
  left to register.

Point a devnet further node at the deployment's reference scripts

A further node has its own reference-script wallet, and the deployment
manifest names the stack node's as the address the reference scripts
were published to. The node refuses a manifest that names another
address, so node 2 stopped at startup with `startup_failed`.

A further node's environment now sets L1_REFERENCE_SCRIPT_DEPLOY_ADDRESS
to the stack node's reference-script wallet, for `listen` and for node
commands.

Verified (rerun here):
- On a devnet run, node 2 started by hand with this setting became
  ready from the empty confirmed ledger, and register-active-operator
  registered and activated its operator (activate tx 7c419dd5...).
- tsc, eslint and prettier on the changed files.

Not verified:
- The changed unit test has not run: the checkout is built for the
  local-devnet-testing profile while the devnet runs, and the test
  setup needs the preprod-testing build.

Run further operators' nodes on a devnet-stack run

A devnet-stack run had exactly one node, so nothing could show a second
operator's node, or a node that joins after blocks have merged, on real
processes.

`up --further-nodes N` fixes N further operators' nodes when the run is
created. The funding transaction pays each one's operator, merge,
reference-script and settlement wallets, the committee's manifests admit
each one's libp2p identity, and each gets its own producer manifest. Both
the funding transaction and the manifests are written once, so the count
cannot change afterwards.

`join-node --node K` starts one of them later, under its own supervisor
with its own database, ledger store, ports and logs, waits until it is
ready and registers its operator. Its LEDGER_SNAPSHOT_PEERS are the run's
other nodes, and every node lists the others in L2_TX_PEERS. `status`
reports further nodes and `down` stops them first.

`da-libp2p-generate-manifest` takes `--admitted-producer` for the
committee target; the library already carried the field.

The devnet genesis supply goes from 2 to 4 billion ADA: one further node
costs 233,680,200 ADA at the existing role budgets and the bootstrap UTxO
had 298,162,300 ADA left.

Verified (rerun here):
- tests/devnet-stack-further-nodes.test.ts: 7 passed, 1 skipped (the
  skipped case needs dists compiled for the local-devnet-testing profile)
- midgard-node-tools tests reached by the changed sources: 850 passed,
  7 skipped
- midgard-node tests reached by index.registration-5.ts: 1419 passed,
  2 skipped
- tsc, eslint and prettier on both packages' changed files

Not verified:
- No devnet run yet: join-node, the committee admitting a further node,
  and a further operator's registration have not run against real
  processes.
- `--admitted-producer` has no test of its own.

Prepare public Preprod API, SDK browser bundling, user CLI, and ops tooling

- Add public-only CORS + OPTIONS preflight across midgard-node and public-ingress.mjs, paginated GET /blocks backed by da_payloads, structured block-hash logging, and raised CLIENT_ACTIVE_MAX (16) and HTTP_READ_LANE_PERMITS (12/2).
- Simplify public node startup in listen-public-http.ts (loopback 127.0.0.1 fallback, opt-in signed release attestation, drop L1_REFERENCE_SCRIPT_SEED_PHRASE from live listen secrets).
- Sever accidental node:* built-in leaks from @al-ft/lucid-midgard and @al-ft/midgard-sdk/users, add MidgardProvider.blocks(), add multi-profile manifest verification for SDK/CLI consumers, add esbuild browser check to sdk-packages.mjs, and make @al-ft/midgard-user-cli publishable with address/balance/send commands and default Blockfrost URLs.
- Add Caddyfile.preprod-public for automatic TLS and single-shot preprod-monitor.mjs for Discord/Slack health and wallet-balance alerts.

Remove milestone labels, history narration and code kept for past designs

Comments, test titles, messages, docs and skills state the rule as it is:
issue numbers, goal and phase labels, ruling labels and accounts of what
the code used to do are gone. File names and identifiers that carried a
label are renamed after what they do.

Code that existed only for a delivered milestone or a past shape is
deleted rather than renamed: the journal kill-recovery harness, the
isolated-chain bootstrap scripts, the phase stress gates and their knobs,
the lettered benchmarks, the ledger-store exit benchmarks, retired CLI
routes and environment-variable guards, one-time table renames, the
migration_version column, unused submit result types, and on-chain
library functions reached only by their own tests.

Every validator keeps its hash and size.

Decide the import checker's deadline tests by a clock the test sets

The late-verdict and saturated-admission tests took a deadline from
`Date.now()`, waited for it on a timer, and then expected the checker,
which reads the wall clock, to have seen it pass. A timer runs on the
monotonic clock. When the wall clock was stepped backward during the wait,
the checker was still short of the deadline at the assertion, and the
missed alarm was absent (`expected [] to deeply equal [...]` at
import-check.late-verdicts.test.ts:151 and
import-check.saturation.test.ts:128).

The saturation test also left its sweep loop running when an assertion
threw. The loop then expired the next test's entry before that test swept,
which is the second failure the same runs show (line 213).

The tests now set the checker's time themselves:

- The late verdict comes from the scripted evaluator, whose run takes the
  test clock from before the deadline to exactly the deadline.
- The saturated pass and its sweeps run on one clock the test sets, with
  real sleeps because the pass waits on a real pool. The test waits for
  the run to be asked for and for admission to finish seven more runs
  after that, then sweeps one millisecond before the deadline (no alarm),
  at it (the alarm) and after it (not again). The pass is settled before
  the test ends, whatever failed.
- The entry "already past its deadline" is an hour past it, as the entries
  not yet due in these suites are an hour ahead.

These tests no longer sleep, and the two files run in about 6 s where
they took about 10 s.

On the machine the failures came from, the kernel log records the wall
clock jumping backward, and every recorded failure of these tests sits
in a run whose log timestamps go backward, in all but one of them by 1.7
to 2.1 s about every 30 s; no run with a steady clock failed. With
`Date.now` replaced in the setup file by a clock that steps back 700 ms
every second (a temporary edit), the old tests failed at the three
assertions above (4 of 9 tests) and the new ones passed 20 runs of 20;
they also passed 20 of 20 on the plain clock. Each of these changes to
checker.ts turns them red: `>=` to `>` on the verdict's deadline check,
`<=` to `<` on the sweep's, and dropping the raised-once guard in
`raiseMissed`.

Install the ledger in the test fixtures that ingest events without a node

A node gives no L1 event a row before its ledger is installed. Four test
files drive event ingestion without starting a node and never installed
one, so their deposits and forced orders got no row. Midgard Node CI
failed on a218a1df4 with six tests in these files.

- `deposit-flow-emulator-shared.ts`: an unowned fixture starts its native
  owner, whose start is the install, before each event ingestion. It was
  started by the first commit worker run, after the first ingestion. Fixes
  `da-bond-pool-bootstrap-emulator` and
  `state-queue-node-floor-challenge-emulator`.
- `forced-order-carriage-emulator.test.ts` and one test of
  `history-commit-window.test.ts` install the empty ledger in their setup.

Test files only; no source change.

Verified (rerun here):
- The four files: 16 passed, 0 failed.
- The 28 test files that import an edited file, directly or through
  another fixture: 50 passed, 0 failed.
- The files `contrib test --related` reaches from every source file this
  branch changed: 238 passed in 34 files.
- tsc --noEmit for midgard-node; eslint and prettier on the three files.

Not verified:
- The whole node suite locally. CI ran it on a218a1df4, where only these
  six tests failed.

Let the acceptance settlement drill outwait and recognise a settlement

The acceptance arms kill-node-on-settlement before the withdrawals phase
submits its orders and gave it 1200 s. On the devnet profile a withdrawal's
settlement starts no sooner than the event wait (300 s) and block maturity
(900 s) after its order, so the wait always ended first: on a live stack
the first settlement transaction appeared 1348 s after arming. The wait is
now the profile's event wait and block maturity plus 25 minutes.

The trigger also listed two details the node stopped reporting in
bc56f0822, and not the one it reports while a settlement transaction is in
a block short of confirmation depth. Four of eleven settlement
transactions on that stack went from checkpointed to landed with no
journaled report between. The node's two wordings now live in
settlement.attempt-detail.ts, and the catalogue test builds its status
bodies from them, so a reworded detail fails the test.

Red before the fix (tests/devnet-stack-chaos.test.ts, 6 passed, 2 failed):
  recognises each targeted moment from the node's status bodies
    expected [ ...(2) ] to deeply equal [ ...(2) ]
    (the landed detail, false against true)
  lets the acceptance wait past the earliest a withdrawal's settlement can
  start
    expected 1200000 to be greater than 1200000

Correct the retention rationale in decision record 0002

The parameter table said parties replay retained payloads from genesis. A
joining node or watcher now replays only the blocks above the confirmed
state; the 120 days stay as set.

Not verified: no doc check beyond prettier was run for this commit.

Remove the late-join limit from the docs

A node with an empty database now takes the confirmed ledger from a node
of the deployment, and a watcher already did. The readiness, security,
threat-model and parameters pages said every party replays from genesis
and that no state snapshot exists; they now say what a joining node or
watcher does and what it needs (one node serving the ledger, and the
retained payloads above the confirmed state).

The stack and e2e pages keep their attach-before-the-first-block flow and
say that joining after a merged block has not been run through the
harness.

Not verified: no doc check or preflight was run for this commit.
